config_name: Steam Deck LCD — Custom AMD 'Aerith' Zen 2 8-core / 8 RDNA1 CUs, 8GB LPDDR5-5500, 256GB NVMe, 7" 1280x800 60Hz IPS

specs.ports: 1x USB-C 3.1 Gen1 (DP alt-mode, PD), microSD UHS-I, 3.5mm
specs.keyboard_notes: no keyboard; on-screen keyboard in SteamOS/Desktop mode
specs.os: SteamOS 3 (Arch Linux + KDE Plasma desktop mode)

battery.notes: 40Wh, 7nm APU. Engadget measured Hades 2h42m on an early LCD; light indie/emu use 4-6h. No fast charge.

price.notes: Verified from steamdeck.com/en 2026-11-24; now the entry-level SKU after Valve's 2025-26 price increases.

reviews.quote: One of the downsides of the first Steam Deck was its short battery life, which maxed out at eight hours, and that was only under ideal conditions.

reviews.outlet: Tom's Guide (original Steam Deck / OLED context)
reviews.quote: The original model was great, but this latest iteration demonstrates that Valve can improve on perfection.

praises: Cheapest entry into SteamOS — same controls, same library, same sleep/resume console UX as the OLED for C$220 less
For emulators, indies and older AAA the 60Hz 400-nit LCD is perfectly fine; many users say the OLED isn't worth upgrading for
iFixit 10/10; the 256GB uses a standard M.2 2230 SSD users commonly swap to 1-2TB themselves
Valve still sells LCD replacement parts (batteries, stick modules, shells) so units are kept alive for years
Frequent Best Buy CA bundle deals make this the value pick of the lineup when discounted
complaints: Battery is the big one — ~2.5-4h in real AAA use; Engadget measured 2h42m in Hades on an early unit
Dim 400-nit glossy LCD washes out outdoors and has visible backlight bleed in dark games vs OLED
60Hz-only display and no HDR — the exact things the OLED fixed
Runs hotter: Engadget's back-to-back test found palms 'breaking a sweat' on the LCD vs the OLED
Wi-Fi 5 and slower 5500 RAM feel dated in 2026; downloads and some stuttering games lag the OLED

design_philosophy: The original 2022 Steam Deck formula — open PC gaming in a console-shaped shell — now repriced as the entry tier after the OLED refresh. The 256GB LCD is Valve's price-of-entry SKU: identical controls and SteamOS, older 7nm APU, dimmer 60Hz LCD, smaller battery.
rating_notes: Ratings inferred from OLED 512GB anchor via SHARED-steam-deck.md LCD deltas: screen_quality −3.0 (400-nit glossy 60Hz IPS vs HDR OLED 90Hz), readability_dark −2.0, readability_bright −1.5, battery −1.0 (40Wh/7nm), thermals_noise −1.0, portability −0.5 (669g), productivity −0.5 (8GB vs 16GB). Pro anchor is Engadget/Tom's Guide LCD-comparison commentary rather than a dedicated 256GB review.
